items.title: OpenAI Launches GPT-6.2 Astra and Sol, Cuts Astra API Prices 20%
items.summary: On November 17, OpenAI released GPT-6.2 Astra and Sol, a two-model split aimed at professional and everyday work respectively. Astra targets complex projects — documents, slides, spreadsheets, code, 3D design and research — and is the company's first released model to reach the 'High' threshold on its AI self-improvement readiness framework. Sol is tuned for efficiency: on Cognition's FrontierCode 2.0 it scored within 0.5 points of Astra at roughly one-fifth the task cost. Astra's API price fell 20% to $8 per million input tokens and $40 per million output tokens, with cached input down 60%; Sol holds at $2/$10. Both are available in ChatGPT Work, Codex and the API, with Ultrafast access expanded to Pro 200 subscribers. Both hit the 'Critical' cyber tier, prompting tighter abuse controls.
items.impact: Price per completed task, not benchmark rank, is the battleground: OpenAI is undercutting rivals just as Anthropic prepares its IPO. The self-improvement threshold is the bigger signal — models are now materially accelerating AI research, forcing new safety gating and monitoring.

items.title: Microsoft Ignite 2026 Unveils Seven MAI Models, Including Code 2 and Cyber 2 Flash
items.summary: At Ignite 2026 in San Francisco on November 17, Microsoft released seven in-house MAI models led by MAI Code 2 and Code 2 Flash for GitHub Copilot, plus MAI Cyber 2 Flash, an image editor, a realtime speech model, a transcription model and a decision model. Microsoft claims Code 2 reaches 98% of GPT-6.1 Sol's coding quality at 40% of the price, and 96% of Claude Opus 5.5's performance at 5% of the cost; Cyber 2 Flash reportedly matches GPT-6 Astra on CyberGymE2E for under 2% of the per-task cost. The company also announced MAI Licensed Weights, letting trusted enterprises fine-tune its models inside their own Azure environments, and said its agentic security system Perception is now generally available.
items.impact: Microsoft is competing on cost-per-agent-hour and control rather than raw frontier scores, with promotional pricing doing much of the work. Licensed weights and in-Azure customization answer enterprise demands for data control — and deepen the lock-in around Foundry and Copilot.

items.title: CISA Flags Actively Exploited Puppet Enterprise RCE Ahead of December 1 Deadline
items.summary: CISA added CVE-2026-115731, a critical deserialization flaw in Perforce Puppet Enterprise, to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog on November 17, citing evidence of active exploitation. The bug sits in Puppet Server's report-processing code: an agent holding a CA-signed certificate can submit a crafted report and run arbitrary code as the Puppet service user. Where certificate auto-signing is enabled without strong checks, an unauthenticated attacker can obtain a certificate first. Rated CVSS 9.4 under v4.0, the flaw was patched on November 3 in Puppet Enterprise 2023.8.13, 2025.12.1 and 2026.0.1, with fixes also in Puppet Core and OpenVox. U.S. federal civilian agencies must remediate by December 1.
items.impact: A compromised Puppet Server can push configuration — and therefore code — to every machine it manages, turning one flaw into fleet-wide compromise. The unauthenticated auto-signing path makes internet-exposed instances urgent, and the two-week gap from patch to KEV listing shows how fast exploitation follows disclosure.

items.title: Citrix NetScaler Zero-Day Chained With RCE Flaw; 20,000+ Instances Exposed
items.summary: Citrix is urging customers to patch CVE-2026-88779, a memory-overflow denial-of-service bug in NetScaler ADC and Gateway being exploited as a zero-day when SAML authentication is combined with Gateway or AAA. Rapid7 says attackers chain it with the RCE flaw CVE-2026-88771 using pre-authentication log poisoning and a SAML-parsing crash. Shadowserver counts more than 20,000 internet-exposed instances potentially at risk, and Google Threat Intelligence and Mandiant found custom 'Whipshot' and 'Slapshot' web shells in intrusions linked to suspected state-linked actors. CISA added the CVE to its KEV catalog and released Sigma detection rules, because attackers wiped local logs on some systems — meaning patching alone may not clean up a compromised appliance.
items.impact: Edge appliances remain a high-leverage target: one device sits in front of many internal systems, and state actors are using them for persistent access. Log-wiping means incident response, not just patching, is required — a hard lesson for teams without offline telemetry.

items.title: Google Splits Gemini Chat History From AI Training — and Extends Retention to Two Months
items.summary: Google is rolling out separate controls in Gemini for chat history and AI-model training, ending the all-or-nothing 'Keep Activity' switch. Users can now keep searchable conversations while opting out of having future chats, including attachments, used to train generative models. Accounts that had Keep Activity off get both new toggles off by default. The trade-off: when History is off, new chats will now be retained for about two months instead of 72 hours (24 hours for conversation context), to answer prompts, process feedback and support safety review. Google says reviewed chats may be kept up to three years and that opting out is not retroactive — earlier training data remains in the models.
items.impact: This is a real win for user control, but the longer hidden retention cuts the other way and shows how 'privacy' settings now balance training consent against safety and abuse detection. Expect regulators to scrutinize the default-off migration and the three-year human-review window.
